content.value_statement: AI image tools often change a character between generations. This skill provides repeatable prompts, reference sheet patterns, and LoRA guidance for consistent visual design.
actual_capabilities: Provides prompt structures for turnaround, expression, outfit, and color palette sheets.
Explains a reusable description anchor technique for character consistency.
Shows belt CLI examples for FLUX LoRA image generation workflows.
Documents common consistency failures and practical prompt fixes.
Includes a character bible template for ongoing visual projects.
limitations: Requires access to the belt CLI and supported image-generation apps for command examples.
Does not guarantee identical faces without trained LoRA or strong reference images.
Outputs depend on the selected image model, seed behavior, and prompt interpretation.
Does not include an automated image review or asset management system.

use_cases.title: Build Game Character References
use_cases.description: Create turnaround views, outfit notes, and color palettes for characters used in game production.

use_cases.title: Plan Comic Cast Consistency
use_cases.description: Use repeated description anchors and expression sheets to keep recurring comic characters recognizable.

use_cases.title: Prepare LoRA Training Assets
use_cases.description: Organize reference images, trigger words, and scale guidance before training character-specific LoRA models.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Character Anchor
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for defining one reusable character description.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to write a 50 word visual anchor for my character. Include age, hair, eyes, skin tone, clothing, shoes, accessories, and one distinctive feature.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Turnaround Sheet Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for planning front, side, back, and three-quarter views.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create prompts for a four-view turnaround sheet. Keep the character description identical and only change the camera angle.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Expression Sheet
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for consistent facial expressions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to produce six expression prompts for the same character: neutral, happy, angry, sad, surprised, and thinking. Preserve facial features and style.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a LoRA Consistency Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a larger project using trained character references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define a character bible and LoRA workflow for a recurring character across many scenes. Include trigger word, scale guidance, and prompt structure.

output_examples.input: I need a reference sheet for a red-haired sci-fi pilot.
output_examples.output: A reusable character anchor, four turnaround prompts, a palette list, and notes for keeping clothing and face details stable.

output_examples.input: My comic character changes age and eye color between images.
output_examples.output: A tighter prompt structure that places age and eye color early, repeats exact descriptors, and records fixed palette values.

output_examples.input: I want to create many scenes with the same protagonist.
output_examples.output: A character bible outline with reference image requirements, a LoRA trigger word, recommended scale range, and scene prompt pattern.

best_practices: Write one detailed visual anchor and reuse it exactly across prompts.
Document colors, proportions, outfits, and facial marks before generating scene variations.
Use LoRA or reference-image workflows for projects that need many consistent images.
anti_patterns: Using vague traits such as young, stylish, or red hair without precise supporting details.
Changing prompt structure each time and expecting stable visual identity.
Creating only one pose before moving into complex scenes or production art.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides prompt and workflow guidance, with examples that use the belt CLI and image-generation apps.

faq.question: Can it keep a character perfectly identical?
faq.answer: No. It improves consistency, but perfect identity usually requires LoRA training, reference images, or model-specific controls.

faq.question: What is a description anchor?
faq.answer: It is a fixed detailed character description that is reused in every prompt to reduce unwanted visual drift.

faq.question: When should I use LoRA?
faq.answer: Use LoRA when a project needs the same character across many images, scenes, or production stages.

faq.question: Is this useful for non-game art?
faq.answer: Yes. It also supports comics, animation, illustration, visual novels, and character concept work.

faq.question: Does it require Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: It can be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as a structured design workflow for AI art prompts.
